players.name: RWE
players.capacity_note: Renewables, batteries and flexible generation (Sept 2025); 11.4 GW under construction; target 65 GW by 2031.
players.mix: Offshore and onshore wind, solar, batteries, gas; lignite in Germany until the legal exit.
players.why: Largest German renewable builder by capacity under construction (11.4 GW), but adjusted EBITDA fell 10 % in 2025. Small in German onshore auctions relative to its size.

players.name: EnBW
players.owner: State of Baden-Württemberg and OEW (municipal association)
players.capacity_note: 65.6 % of capacity renewable; 25.7 TWh generated, 13.6 TWh renewable.
players.markets: Mainly Germany; offshore wind also in the UK
players.mix: Renewables 7.4 GW; hydrogen-ready gas plants replacing coal (Stuttgart-Münster, Heilbronn, Altbach); last lignite stake (Lippendorf) sold.
players.why: Earnings up, net debt down by €1.1bn, offshore wind He Dreiht feeding in since Nov 2025. Grid business carries more than half of EBITDA.

players.name: Vattenfall
players.capacity_note: Generation 102.1 TWh: nuclear 39 %, hydro 37 %, wind 17 %, fossil 7 %.
players.mix: Nuclear and hydro (Sweden), wind on- and offshore, fossil 7 % of output; growth capex 2026–30 mainly wind (SEK 59bn of 92bn).
players.why: Strong balance sheet, final investment decision on Nordlicht offshore (Germany's largest wind project), but little new capacity in 2025.

players.name: Uniper
players.owner: German federal government (rescued 2022; reprivatisation started 2026, state to keep 25 % + 1 share)
players.capacity_note: European generation: gas 11.2 GW, hydro 3.6 GW, coal 2.3 GW, nuclear (Sweden) 1.4 GW.
players.markets: Germany, Sweden, UK, Netherlands, Hungary and others; global gas and LNG trading
players.mix: Gas-heavy fleet plus hydro and Swedish nuclear; coal exit planned by 2029, Datteln 4 must be sold by end 2026; hydrogen import terminal planned in Wilhelmshaven; renewables (Green Generation) small but growing.
players.why: Adjusted EBITDA fell 58 % to €1.1bn after the crisis-era windfall; about 400 jobs cut; ownership in flux. Not a bidder in German onshore or solar auctions under its own name.

players.name: EWE
players.group_note: Wins German wind auctions through Alterric (50 % joint venture), shown separately.
players.owner: Municipalities in north-west Germany (74 %) and Ardian (26 %)
players.markets: Germany, Poland, Turkey (gas and grids); wind via Alterric in Germany, France, Greece
players.mix: Grids, gas and electricity supply, telecoms; wind through Alterric; hydrogen projects in the north-west.
players.why: Operating EBIT down 10 % on a weak wind year; investment raised to €1.6bn.

players.name: Statkraft
players.mix: Mostly Norwegian hydro (51 of 72 TWh in 2025); onshore wind, solar and district heating;
players.why: Record output and NOK 12bn less net debt in 2025.

players.name: LEAG
players.mix: Lignite mines and power plants; building solar and wind on former mining land (target 7 GW by 2030, 14 GW by 2040) and large batteries (Jänschwalde 1 GW / 4 GWh, Boxberg 400 MW / 1.6 GWh).
players.why: A lignite company turning its mining land into a renewables and storage hub ('GigawattFactory').

players.name: Alterric
players.owner: EWE and Aloys Wobben Stiftung (Enercon owner), 50/50
players.capacity_note: Own wind portfolio; target up to 5 GW by 2030.
players.why: One of the fastest-rising groups in German wind auctions; corporate credit line raised to €350m.

players.name: Qualitas Energy
players.capacity_note: Operating and development assets; €4.6bn raised across funds since inception.
players.markets: Spain, Germany, UK, Italy, Poland, US, Chile
players.mix: Onshore wind, solar, storage; repowering of old German wind farms.
players.why: Grew in Germany by buying developers and pipelines (DunoAir, PNE portfolio); biggest share gain in German wind auctions.

players.name: Enerparc
players.owner: Founders (insolvency administrator in charge since Sept 2026)
players.capacity_note: Solar in operation; 1.5 GW under construction; target was 10 GW own + 10 GW third party by 2030.
players.markets: More than 25 countries (projects built); own portfolio mainly Germany
players.mix: Solar, solar-plus-storage; EPC, O&M and power marketing (Sunnic).
players.why: Largest solar auction winner; filed for insolvency in Sept 2026 after a financing for solar-plus-storage failed.

players.name: UKA
players.mix: Onshore wind and solar; develops, builds and sells to investors.
players.turbines: Ordered 226 Nordex turbines (more than 1.5 GW) in 18 months to June 2025, then about 700 MW more in July 2026.
players.why: Largest winner of German onshore wind auctions since 2019; framework agreement with Nordex.

players.name: wpd
players.capacity_note: 2,810 turbines built; 3.5 GW kept in its own portfolio.
players.mix: Onshore and offshore wind, some solar.
players.why: Rising share in German wind auctions; about 1 GW under construction in Germany.

players.name: JUWI
players.capacity_note: Wind and solar realised since 1996 (more than 3,000 units).
players.markets: Germany, US, Australia, South Africa, Greece and others
players.mix: Onshore wind and solar development, EPC and O&M.
players.why: Wins in about three of four German wind rounds since its first award.

players.name: PNE
players.owner: Listed; Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners largest shareholder
players.markets: Germany and Europe; exited the US, UK and Sweden
players.mix: Onshore wind, solar, storage; growing own portfolio ('Scale up').
players.why: Record revenue and 428 MW sold in 2025, but a net loss from write-downs abroad; now focusing on core markets.

players.name: Energiekontor
players.capacity_note: 40 own parks (455 MW) plus about 230 MW under construction for the own portfolio; about half of projects kept, half sold.
players.why: Cut its 2025 profit target from €70–90m to €30–40m because of delays in Germany and the UK; losing share in German wind auctions.

players.name: ABO Energy
players.mix: Wind, solar, storage, hybrid and hydrogen; develops and sells (e.g. 4.4 GW Finnish wind pipeline to Fortum, 2025).
players.why: First-ever loss (about €170m for 2025); out-of-court restructuring with a bank standstill to 30 Nov 2026.

players.name: ENERTRAG
players.capacity_note: Wind and solar in operation; own 660 km grid in the Uckermark.
players.mix: Onshore wind, solar, own grid, green hydrogen (Prenzlau, Heidekrautbahn trains).
players.why: Rising share in German wind auctions; integrates wind, grid and hydrogen in one region.

players.name: BayWa r.e.
players.owner: BayWa AG (51 % stake planned for sale) and Energy Infrastructure Partners
players.markets: Europe and the Americas; left Asia-Pacific
players.mix: Solar and wind development, solar wholesale, power trading.
players.why: EBIT of −€732m in 2024; new 2026–28 plan missed targets, so the parent's restructuring concept had to be redone (Mar 2026).
